name: Ireland
sources: GDP $49.3bn and population 3.51m: World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD and SP.POP.TOTL, series IRL, 1990 (49,305,632,408 and 3,513,974). Same series as the rest of the roster, and the smallest economy in it after Kuwait's. Ireland in 1990 is a poor country by Western European standards - output per head around two-thirds of the Community average, unemployment near 13%, and net emigration of about 1% of the population a year, the last time that was true anywhere in Western Europe.
Inflation 3.3%: World Bank FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG, IRL 1990 = 3.317%. The punt had been in the ERM since 1979, when Ireland broke the sterling link it had held since 1826.

Policy rate 11.3%: three-month Dublin interbank rate, monthly mean of 1990 = 11.307% (OECD MEI via FRED, IR3TIB01IEM156N). Well above German and Dutch rates on the same mechanism, which is the risk premium a small currency with an 86%-of-GDP debt paid; the punt was devalued 10% in January 1993 after a two-month defence at penal rates.

Gross public debt 86% of GDP: IMF Historical Public Debt Database, central government debt, IRL 1990 = 86.3%. CAVEAT: this is the CENTRAL government measure - the IMF WEO general-government series does not carry Ireland back to 1990 - and the general-government figure for 1990 is higher, in the low nineties on the AMECO basis. A floor rather than a like-for-like figure, recorded so the basis is visible rather than assumed. Either way it is the second-worst debt in this batch after Belgium's 1.30, and the fiscal correction of 1987-89 that brought it down from a peak above 110% is the immediate background to every Irish figure in this file.
Revenue 33% of GDP: OECD Revenue Statistics, total tax revenue as a share of GDP, Ireland 1990 (about 32.5%).
Military 1.2% of GDP: World Bank MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS (SIPRI), IRL 1990 = 1.204%, the joint lowest in Western Europe with Austria's.

Strength index 2: the smallest armed force on the board. About 13,000 in the Permanent Defence Force, no tanks beyond a handful of armoured cars, no interceptor aircraft, no submarines, and a naval service of seven patrol vessels for fishery protection. Indexed at an eighth of Spain's 16 and a third of Denmark's 6 - Denmark is a comparable-sized NATO state and has a real armoured brigade and a real navy. Ireland is militarily neutral, was never in NATO, and its army's actual employment since 1958 has been United Nations peacekeeping, in Lebanon in 1990. A 2 is not an insult; it is what a state that has genuinely decided not to have a military looks like in an index.

Gross fixed capital formation 19.2% of GDP: World Bank NE.GDI.FTOT.ZS, IRL 1990 - the lowest in this batch, and the reason is the fiscal correction: public capital spending had been cut hard. Split into public 2.2% and private 17.0% using the AMECO general-government series, private as residual. CAVEAT: total transcribed, public share entered from reference knowledge of AMECO.

Stability 72 and authoritarianism 0.11: below the United Kingdom's 74 and above Italy's 68. Charles Haughey's Fianna Fail-Progressive Democrats cabinet, formed in July 1989, was the first coalition Fianna Fail had ever entered in sixty-three years - the party's founding claim was that it alone could govern alone, and 1989 ended it. The Northern Ireland conflict was at its height across the border: 1990 saw 76 deaths, the IRA bombing campaign extended to Great Britain and Germany, and the Republic's own security apparatus - the Special Criminal Court, sitting without a jury, and section 31 of the Broadcasting Act, which banned Sinn Fein spokesmen from Irish radio and television until 1994 - is the reason authoritarianism is 0.11 rather than the 0.08 the Nordic democracies carry.

Separatism 0.02: low, and the direction matters. Ireland's territorial question in 1990 ran outward, not inward - Articles 2 and 3 of the 1937 Constitution claimed the whole island - and that is entered as a CLAIM on the United Kingdom in the roster, not as separatism here. There is no movement to detach any part of the twenty-six counties from Dublin.

TFP trend 0.020: the top of the roster's range, above Germany's 0.016 and Finland's 0.017, and it is the only number in this batch that needs defending as high rather than as low. Irish GDP grew at an average of about 7% a year from 1994 to 2000 and total factor productivity growth over the decade was the fastest in the OECD. The ingredients were all in place by January 1990 - a 10% manufacturing corporation tax rate in force since 1981, the Programme for National Recovery social partnership agreement of 1987, European structural funds, and a young English-speaking workforce that emigration had until then been exporting. Entering an average European number here would make the model unable to produce the one thing everybody knows about Ireland in this period.

pop_growth_1990 = -0.1215%/yr. Compound annual growth of World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series IRL (Ireland): 3,532,423 in 1984 to 3,511,009 in 1989 — the five years ending on the eve of the 1 January 1990 start date. See EconomyRecord::pop_growth_1990 in spheres-sim/src/data/mod.rs for why the window ends in 1989 and not with the single-year 1990 rate.

reserves_bn = 4.201 ($bn). Total reserves including gold, IRL, 1989: US$4201462260.95 (World Bank World Development Indicators series FI.RES.TOTL.CD, 'Total reserves (includes gold, current US$)', retrieved from the World Bank API on 2026-09-02; indicator lastupdated 2026-07-13). THE 1989 OBSERVATION AND NOT THE 1990 ONE: a reserve is a stock, and the stock on the morning of the 1 January 1990 start date is the end-1989 figure - the same reasoning pop_growth_1990 above gives for ending its window on 31 December 1989. LIMIT STATED: this series is official reserve assets. Sovereign wealth fund balances are not in it and none has been added, because no audited 1990 balance could be sourced for any of them; where that materially understates a state's usable stock it is reported rather than estimated (iron rule 4).

note: 1990 TECHNOLOGY: AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED. What this nation knew on 1 January 1990 is transcribed and sourced grant by grant, exactly like every other 1990 figure in this file, and is not read off tfp_trend - there was never a code path from the trend to the known set, and the zero that stood there was a claim about the world rather than an absence of one (BIBLE section 8 and iron rule 4, both amended 2026-08-30). THE PREDICATE IS SPLIT, and split by the technology's OWN EFFECT TYPE so that it is mechanically computable and never a per-nation judgement call. A node whose effects include MilitaryEfficiency, MilitaryStrength, DiffusionEmission or CostReduction is SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE: holding it means this nation could PRODUCE it, so operating an imported article does not qualify. Every other node is USE-SIDE: deployed and in operational use here is enough, whoever built it, because the effect such a node pays is a productivity, health or output effect and that effect is real in the country where the machine runs. Of the 48 technologies the tree lets anyone hold in 1990, 17 are sovereignty-side and 31 are use-side.

DATA-KEYED TAIL NATION. This nation is outside the 29 authored majors, so nothing here was authored technology by technology: a grant is made only where one of two named published global series supports it, and nothing is modelled, estimated or interpolated. A short list, or an empty one, is the correct outcome of that rule and not a gap in the work.

Data-keyed tail nation: not one of the 29 authored majors. Only the two series named in ruling 3 were consulted - WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 1990 and World Bank IT.CEL.SETS. Nothing was modelled, estimated or interpolated, and no other evidence was admitted. ISO3 key used for both series: IRL.
WUENIC DTP3 1990 = 65% against the 80% UCI-1990 threshold: refused.
IT.CEL.SETS at 31 December 1989 = 13579 against a threshold of any positive count: comm_cellular_analogue GRANTED.

The other 46 grantable 1990 technologies are BLANK for this nation by design, not by oversight: the 17 sovereignty-side entries are unreachable by any use-in-operation series, and no published global series was named that keys the remaining 29 use-side entries.

granted.source: World Bank WDI IT.CEL.SETS 'Mobile cellular subscriptions', retrieved from the World Bank indicator API (api.worldbank.org/v2), source id 2, lastupdated 2026-07-13. Series values: IRL, 1989 = 13579 subscriptions and 1990 = 25000 subscriptions. The series is a YEAR-END STOCK, so the 1989 figure describes 31 December 1989, i.e. the game's start instant of 1 January 1990: a network was carrying paying subscribers before the start date. All cellular in service at that date was analogue (NMT, AMPS, TACS, C-Netz, RTMS); GSM had no commercial service anywhere until mid-1991.
